items_missed: No 'How are you today?' — went straight from name to 'how can I help you?'
No agenda statement with a time estimate and no 'sound good?' confirmation; the only framing came mid-call ('I'll go ahead and explain the pricing then the estimate')
Never checked or stated availability for the Feb 1 date — only confirmed the requested date was correct
Never asked about garage / storage unit / balcony contents at the origin house
Never asked about packing services — the customer had to raise it himself at the end of the call
Never asked the stressor question ('anything you're particularly worried about with this move?')
No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) never mentioned
Meet Your Mover email never mentioned
Never explained that the clock starts on-site when the contract opens
Estimate never cited the ~100 ft walk distance as a time variable even though she collected it
No booking attempt at all — never asked to lock the Feb 1 date in
Never described the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email or asked the customer to reply with corrections
No business hours given — just 'give us a call anytime'
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped (prep = shorter move = lower bill, consolidation examples, carload tip)
top_strength: Excellent, disciplined intake on a genuinely messy job — she untangled a partial-house move plus a second pickup at the girlfriend's apartment, and pinned down floor, elevator, parking, stair-to-door distance, oversized items, and box counts for both stops. The estimate she built off it (4.5-6.5 hrs, $1,086-$1,502) is well-reasoned and clearly tied to the extra stop and the third-floor destination.
coaching_note: The three differentiators are the whole pitch and Danah gave none of them — No Worries coverage, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee all need to land right after the hourly rate. Second: she never asked for the booking. Casey was a warm, ready buyer with a specific date and she ended on 'I'll email it to you.'
phone_presence_notes: Polite and organized with steady name use and a warm close (customer volunteered 'I appreciate you'), but the language is transactional — heavy 'mm-hmm' filler, no empathy statements, no humor, and she plows from question to question without reacting to what Casey says.
